items.name: Adult Disability Payment

value.description: Must have a long-term physical or mental health condition or disability that affects daily living or mobility for at least 13 weeks and is expected to last at least 9 more months.

items.text: Must have a long-term physical or mental health condition or disability that affects daily living or mobility for at least 13 weeks and is expected to last at least 9 more months.

problems.claim: Must have a long-term physical or mental health condition or disability that affects daily living or mobility for at least 13 weeks and is expected to last at least 9 more months.
problems.note: The text supports the condition affecting everyday life, but it does not mention the 13-week or 9-month periods.
problems.quote: Adult Disability Payment is extra money to help you if you have a disability or long-term health condition that affects your everyday life.

quotes.quote: Adult Disability Payment is extra money to help you if you have a disability or long-term health condition that affects your everyday life.

items.action: Cite the official eligibility guidance for the 13-week and 9-month condition duration rules.
items.reason: The duration test is a core qualifying rule, so if it were wrong, people with recent or short-term conditions would be told wrongly whether they qualify.

items.name: Young Carer Grant
items.text: You can apply or do this online. You can apply or do this by phone.

problems.note: The text mentions filling in a form but does not say the form is online.
problems.quote: You'll need to fill in a new form or call us each year you want to apply.

quotes.quote: You'll need to fill in a new form or call us each year you want to apply.

items.action: Cite the official page that confirms the Young Carer Grant can be applied for online.
items.reason: Anyone told to apply online would be sent the wrong way if online isn't actually an option, and applying is the main thing people use this service for.

items.name: NHS 111 online
items.value: Free for anyone in England, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Use NHS 111 when you need medical help fast but the situation is not life-threatening. The service assesses your symptoms and advises whether to go to A&E, see a GP urgently, visit a pharmacy, or treat yourself at home.
items.text: Free for anyone in England, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Use NHS 111 when you need medical help fast but the situation is not life-threatening. The service assesses your symptoms and advises whether to go to A&E, see a GP urgently, visit a pharmacy, or treat yourself at home.

problems.note: The text does not mention cost.

problems.claim: It is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
problems.note: The text does not give opening hours.

problems.claim: Use NHS 111 when you need medical help fast but the situation is not life-threatening.
problems.note: The text covers needing help right now, but says nothing about the situation not being life-threatening.
problems.quote: If you think you need medical help right now, 111 online can tell you what to do next.

problems.claim: The service assesses your symptoms and advises whether to go to A&E, see a GP urgently, visit a pharmacy, or treat yourself at home.
problems.note: The text says it directs you to the best place, but it does not list A&E, an urgent GP visit, a pharmacy or self-care at home as outcomes.
problems.quote: we will direct you to the best place to get help for your symptoms

quotes.quote: If you think you need medical help right now, 111 online can tell you what to do next.
we will direct you to the best place to get help for your symptoms

items.action: Cite official sources that say the service is free, runs 24/7, covers England and is for non-life-threatening situations, and that list the possible outcomes.
items.reason: Unsourced claims about cost, opening hours, who can use it and when it is appropriate could change whether a typical person decides to use 111 or call 999.

items.name: Adult Disability Payment
items.value: Scotland's replacement for Personal Independence Payment (PIP). For adults aged 16+ (under State Pension age) with a long-term physical or mental health condition or disability. Same rates as PIP. Assessed on impact of condition, not the condition itself.
items.text: Scotland's replacement for Personal Independence Payment (PIP). For adults aged 16+ (under State Pension age) with a long-term physical or mental health condition or disability. Same rates as PIP. Assessed on impact of condition, not the condition itself.

problems.claim: It is Scotland's replacement for Personal Independence Payment (PIP).
problems.note: The text describes moving from PIP to Adult Disability Payment but does not call Adult Disability Payment PIP's replacement.
problems.quote: you’ve moved from Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) Personal Independence Payment (PIP) to Adult Disability Payment

problems.claim: It is for adults aged 16 or over who are under State Pension age.
problems.note: The text gives no age limits for Adult Disability Payment; the only '16 or over' is for the vehicle leasing scheme.

problems.claim: It is paid at the same rates as PIP.
problems.note: The text never compares the rates with PIP.

quotes.quote: Adult Disability Payment is extra money to help you if you have a disability or long-term health condition that affects your everyday life.
The amount you get depends on how your condition affects your ability to do everyday activities and get around.
you’ve moved from Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) Personal Independence Payment (PIP) to Adult Disability Payment

items.action: Cite the official page for the age limits (16 to State Pension age), noting the exception for existing claimants over State Pension age.
items.reason: The age band decides who can apply, so if it were wrong, people would be told wrongly whether they qualify.
